newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-U.S. rate hike, bonds may help Lisbon shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-U.S. rate hike, bonds may help Lisbon shares.

text.p: Lisbon share prices could benefit in the medium term from a rise in U.S. interest rates, a buoyant Portuguese bond market and the privatisation of Portugal's biggest cement firm Cimpor, analysts said on Tuesday.

Dealers and analysts were deeply divided over whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) would sanction a credit tightening after a meeting at 1300 GMT, the outcome of which would not be known until after European markets closed. If the Fed decided to increase interest rates, it would be the first rise for 1-1/2 years.

"The initial impact of a U.S. rate rise on Lisbon shares could be negative if European markets fall, although the markets may have discounted the impact already," said Isabel Cabral, economist with Lisbon broker Fincor.
"However, the longer term impact should be positive as a stronger dollar would mean it would be cheaper for U.S. investment funds to buy Lisbon shares."
Analysts estimate that U.S. funds account for more than half of foreign investment on Lisbon bourse.
A U.S. rate rise could push up the value of the dollar as the return on U.S.-denominated assets increases.
Sally Wilkinson, an economist with UBS in London, said she believed that European markets had already discounted a U.S. rate hike.
But she said the buoyant Portuguese bond market, lifted by optimism that Portugal would qualify to join the European single currency, could feed through eventually into the share market.
"The bond market is a very supportive factor for Lisbon shares," she said.
Lisbon shares have largely ignored the sharp drops in other European markets in recent days amid fears that a rise in U.S. rates could cause Wall Street to dive.

The BVL30 index of 30 leading shares on the Lisbon bourse has already risen by 24 percent since the start of 1996 and analysts said the market could rise by up to five percent during the rest of the year if the U.S. raises its rates soon.
Wilkinson said a possible further cut in the Portuguese repo rate to 7.00 percent from 7.25 percent by early November, after the October 15 budget, could also help Portuguese share prices.
Another factor that could drive up shares in the coming months was the sale of a 45 percent stake in state cement firm Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal SA on October 15, analysts said.

"Investment funds may sell some shares in order to buy Cimpor ahead of the privatisation. But after the sale Cimpor will become a very liquid stock capable of driving the market," said Mark Howard of Lloyds Bank Fund Managers in Cascais.

Analysts polled by Reuters said they were optimistic that the privatisation of cash-rich Cimpor, which could be worth more than 120 billion escudos ($776 million), would be comfortably oversubscribed.
